si_thresholds: hypotension (SBP under 90), tachycardia (HR over 120), tachypnea (RR over 24), or hypoxia (SpO2 under 90%)
significant peripheral edema, pulmonary edema on chest imaging, or elevated JVP
end-organ dysfunction (acute kidney injury, elevated natriuretic peptides, elevated troponin)
NYHA class III-IV symptoms, orthopnea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea
cardiogenic shock with hypoperfusion or need for inotropes/vasopressors
is_requirements: intravenous diuretics with continuous or frequent bolus dosing and strict intake/output monitoring
intensive monitoring (telemetry, frequent vitals, daily weights, strict I/O)
renal replacement therapy or ultrafiltration for refractory overload
two_midnight_expectation: Typical stay 4-7 days when intravenous diuretics are required; shorter stays possible for patients responsive to a single IV diuretic dose with stable vitals; longer for cardiogenic shock or refractory overload.
denial_downgrade_triggers: single IV diuretic dose with rapid improvement
chronic stable heart failure without acute exacerbation
dispositional issues (awaiting placement) without ongoing active treatment
overturn_support_factors: documented diuretic resistance and failure of outpatient oral diuretics
documented monitoring needs (daily weights, strict I/O, electrolyte/renal monitoring)
high readmission risk (recent hospitalizations, poor adherence, no follow-up)
complicating comorbidities (CKD, diabetes, COPD, atrial fibrillation)
